notes: Status partial. The task asked for the WFSA's current database totals: the WFSA still keeps the database (home page, Oct 2026) but has published no totals after its peer-reviewed 2000-2014 tally (Golden and Weisbrod 2016: 232 accidents of two or more deaths, 21,574 dead and missing, 1,541 a year), repeated for 2000-2015 in its Jan 2017 Marine News column. That tally is entered as ferry-wfsa-2000-2014 (grade B). The only yearly series found is the trade publication Baird Maritime's Passenger Vessel Accident Database, printed once a year in an editorial: 2020 264 deaths (20 accidents), 2021 1,380 (26; later restated 1,378 and 25), 2022 699 (41), 2023 1,308 (39), 2024 2,033 (55), 2025 1,455 (50). Six rows, grade C: the publisher produced the figures (so the editorials are the primary printing) but it is press, publishes no method, source list or table, and the task wanted a table or report. The same database underlies the LRF 2018 insight report, the WMU 2023 scoping study and an IMO 2023 concept paper, which repeats Baird's 2020 and 2021 totals as 'dead or missing'. Definitions: Baird's editorials define neither ferry nor death. Its compiler's 2018 thesis (ferry-baird-2000-2015-average, grade B; an examined thesis, downgrade to C if the lab does not accept theses) defines a ferry as 'A vessel carrying paying passengers on a regular service on a defined route', counts 'known' fatalities from reports, does not say whether missing persons are included, and excludes refugee and migrant boat deaths. The database covers ferries, tour boats and cruise ships, and the 2025 count holds a homicide and an apparently self-inflicted death, so it is not an accidental-death or drowning count. WFSA counts dead and missing in accidents with two or more deaths, from news reports, investigation reports and GISIS. What the counts leave out: accidents nobody reported (Baird: 'the real situation can safely be assumed to be significantly worse'; the thesis puts true figures at least 50 per cent higher); Myanmar and North Korea (no data); single-death accidents (WFSA threshold); refugee and migrant boats (Baird); cargo, fishing, work boats and private small craft (both). Country figures for DR Congo, Nigeria, Bangladesh, Indonesia, Madagascar and Mozambique are printed in the editorials and recorded in notes only; they were not entered as rows and were never added to anything. Disagreements recorded, not reconciled: 2021 printed as 1,380/26 (Feb 2022) then 1,378/25 (Feb 2023, Feb 2024), kept as a low-high pair in one row; the editorial of 16 Jan 2025 labels the Congolese figure (950/11) and the Nigerian one (423/13) as 2023 while that of 8 Jan 2026 labels the same numbers 2024 (and they exceed the 2023 total, so 2024 is right); WFSA's 1,541 a year (2000-2014, two-death threshold) against the thesis's 1,975 a year (2000-2015) from the same era; LRF's 750 fatal passenger-vessel accidents and 59,600 deaths for 1966-2015 against the thesis's 681 ferry accidents and nearly 60,000. Two corrections are proposed, both to notes: ferry-wfsa (its open task is now answered as far as public documents allow) and water-transport-other (what the only series excludes). The Baird 2025 row cites the AMP address that was opened; the canonical address drops '/amp/story'. The thesis URL carries the author's surname as part of the file name, as the publisher hosts it; the citation is by surname, as the ledger does for papers. No names, contact details or precise positions were recorded. GISIS was not opened (login). VERIFICATION 21 Oct 2026: all eight figures confirmed as printed; the thesis row regraded C; the thesis PDF's file name on the publisher's site carries the author's name, as academic citations do (the ledger already cites authors by surname), flagged for the maintainer's PII judgment; the Jan 2025 and Jan 2026 editorials label the DR Congo and Nigeria accidents as 2023 and 2024 respectively, left unresolved.
